text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Pakistan's Interior Minister Naseerullah Babar visited Kabul, Kandahar and Mazar-i-Sharif and held talks with Taleban leaders and Uzbek militia leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum on a possible peace deal.
- A four-member team of Pakistan's top economic managers began talks with the International Monetary Fund on a new economic reform package proposed by Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's government.
- A student demonstration turned into a riot in Lahore when police barred protesters from marching to the Governor's House.
- The Pakistani High Commission has postponed two investment conferences Pakistan was to have held in Britain.
- Authorities suspended a senior police officer involved in the alleged gunbattle in which Murtaza Bhutto, estranged brother of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto, was shot dead.
- The government might impose a quarterly export quota for cotton amid conflicting reports about the exportable surplus.
- The World Bank will use its connections with telecom operators and investors to generate interest in the sale of a 26 percent stake in state-run Pakistan Telecommunication Co Ltd.
- Current spending grew 98 percent in the past six years, while income expanded only 91 percent, a main reason for the widening budget deficit, Islamabad Stock Exchange president Tariq Iqbal said.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan may halt further credit to the Sindh provincial government, whose overdraft has reached a record high of nearly seven billion rupees.
- An executive of Pakistan's United Bank Limited was extradited from Dubai to face fraud charges in Karachi.
- The World Bank warned that it would stop financial aid to developing countries that do not crack down on corruption.
